name: ioprio_set
synopsis: int syscall(SYS_ioprio_set, int which, int who, int ioprio);
Note: glibc provides no wrappers for these system calls, necessitating the use of syscall(2).
description: The ioprio_set() system call sets the I/O scheduling class and priority of one or more threads. It identifies the target threads using the 'which' and 'who' arguments and applies the specified I/O priority.

parameters.name: which
parameters.description: Determines how 'who' is interpreted, such as IOPRIO_WHO_PROCESS, IOPRIO_WHO_PGRP, or IOPRIO_WHO_USER

parameters.name: who
parameters.description: Identifies the thread(s) to operate on, depending on the value of 'which'

parameters.name: ioprio
parameters.description: A bit mask specifying the I/O scheduling class and priority to assign

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set to indicate the error

errors.description: Invalid value for which or ioprio
The calling process does not have the required privilege to assign the I/O priority
No process(es) could be found that matched the specification in which and who

bugs: glibc does not yet provide a suitable header file defining the function prototypes and macros described on this page.
